quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake suddenly. What usually causes this?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading
The front wheel is not tightened properly to the frame
Hitting an object with the front tire

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards
It prevents you from finding an escape route
It gives you space to maneuver your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely. Space helps you find escape routes, not prevents them.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic
questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you
Provide a wide view of the road behind you
Are illegal

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters
Blue with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show service locations. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time
Only brake
Do one action, then the other

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: When you must swerve and brake, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: What is a primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions
Turning too wide in a curve or turn
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn
questions.explanation: Turning too wide in a curve or turn is a primary cause of single-vehicle crashes. Taking a turn too wide can make a motorcycle leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so
Only stop to yield to other traffic
Vehicles will be entering the roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about motorized scooters is correct?

options.text: Can only be operated during the day
Can be operated without a driver license
Can be operated with any class of driver license

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be operated with any class of driver license
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you instead of the center of the lane. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What must a helmet have for riders under age 21?

options.text: Reflective material.
Hearing protection.
Yellow color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective material.
questions.explanation: Riders under 21 must wear an approved helmet with a chin or neck strap. The helmet must have reflective material on both sides with at least four square inches of reflection, unless the helmet is made of reflective material.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Stop completely.
You can go through with caution.
Yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Right side
Center
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side might make the other driver move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have space to maneuver.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle helps you react to problems and maneuver safely if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead.
Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. A signal left on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, ride in:

options.text: The left side of your lane.
The right side of your lane.
The center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on the right. This helps you avoid opening doors and people stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center to have space on both sides.

questions.question: Before turning, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent power changes during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting while turning can cause the rear wheel to suddenly change power and skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route.
Help you feel wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you feel wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you know about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Only ride on it if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It usually gives good traction, except when it is raining.
Always avoid it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good traction, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road is often oily but usually provides enough traction for safe riding when it is dry. When it rains, traction is reduced. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Right side
Center
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left side
questions.explanation: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It is connected to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When you need to react to a hazard in the road, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers you are there.
Change your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to let others know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers you are there.
questions.explanation: To stay safe and reduce danger, let other drivers know you are there. Use your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to match the situation. Change your lane position or direction if needed.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when you enter a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve
On the inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When should you keep a greater distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through the vehicles in front to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance to at least four seconds when the road is slippery, when you cannot see ahead through other vehicles, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake.
The front and rear brakes at the same time.
Only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal, non-emergency stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center portion of the lane is the safest place to ride. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What may give you poor traction while riding?

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The road under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Traction may be poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates or utility hole covers.
